findings.title: The resolver's JSON and error envelopes sit outside the one contract source
findings.claim: `plugin/scripts/planroom` is a hand-written POSIX sh script. It emits public agent-facing JSON: the `engine_fetching` and `engine_unavailable` envelopes, and `status --json`, which the mod's `engine` atom and S14 depend on. None of that output is generated from `planroom-contract`, and no test validates it against the schema. That breaks the one-source constraint, the 'one versioned schema behind them all' principle and the design's own rule that error codes are spelled in exactly one place.
findings.evidence: contracts.md:70, the 'Resolver environment and status' row: single source `plugin/scripts/planroom and the table`, codegen targets `none`, and its drift tests are only behavioural (`tests/installer/run.sh::base_url_refuses...`, `status_names_the_step_that_resolved`). contracts.md:173-174 define `engine_fetching` and `engine_unavailable` as 'the resolver's envelope'. contracts.md:150 says '`contract::ErrorCode` is the only place a code is spelled; a source scan fails on a code string anywhere else.' architecture.md:1427 (fetch lock) has the sh script 'exit non-zero with one envelope'. Architecture 'Mod > Wiring' step 2 stores the resolver's output in `$.state planroom.engine`. This conflicts with KICKOFF <constraints> 'One contract source. Schemas for the store, API, CLI `--json` output, tools and packs are generated for every language from one source, with a drift test. Never hand-copy types across the language boundary', and with principle 2: 'stable error codes and one versioned schema behind them all'.
findings.failure_scenario: During S14 step 2 ('The engine resolves on first use'), an agent driving S1 through a skill's Bash call hits the 20 s lock and receives the shell's `engine_fetching` JSON. A contributor later renames `details.fix` to `details.command` in the Rust registry, or adds a required `meta.size`. The sh template keeps the old shape, and no test notices, because `every_cli_json_output_validates` runs only on Rust CLI outputs. The agent then parses an envelope that doesn't match `Envelope`, or the mod reads a `status --json` field that no longer exists and draws the wrong fallback pane. The alternative is just as bad: `errors_are_only_built_from_the_registry` flags the sh literals and the code gets exempted, after which the codes drift unnoticed.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `ResolverStatus` and the two resolver envelopes (as `Envelope<()>` with `ErrorObject`) as `$defs` in `planroom-contract`. Have `cargo xtask gen` write a generated `plugin/scripts/contract.sh` holding `SCHEMA_VERSION`, the code, category, exit and retry constants, and printf templates. The resolver sources that file and never spells a code itself. Add `tests/installer/run.sh::every_resolver_output_validates`, which checks each resolver stdout (status, `engine_fetching`, `engine_unavailable` for each reason) against the committed schema. Scope the source scan so codes may appear only in generated files.

findings.title: Pane flows need three to four keystrokes, so S9's two-key bar fails
findings.claim: The design adds a confirming card after the action key for paid steps and repo-changing steps. On any row except the first, running a plan stage or starting a hand-off from the pane then takes three or more real presses. S9's own assertion includes 'acting on the last visible row of each list', so it fails. The cost card is also a redundant interruption: the person has already consented to the provider, the spend is within the daily budget, and pressing Enter was the decision.
findings.evidence: architecture.md:1020: 'Enter on a stage row runs `intent next --stage S`. That can spend, so the engine deals its cost card first and the card's pick confirms it, as for every paid step.' architecture.md:1268, Row keys: 'A row key selects its row, and an action key then acts on the selected row... acting on any visible row takes at most two keys.' Pane table: `h` hand off; 'A repo-changing ... step ... opens its card in the pane, where confirming takes a second, deliberate key.' feature_list.json S9 asserts 'every action in the scripted flows is at most two real key presses from pane focus, on any visible row' and lists the step 'including acting on the last visible row of each list' and 'Enter on a stage row under i'. KICKOFF S9: 'Every action is at most two keystrokes from pane focus.' Principle 1: 'Interrupt a person only for decisions only they can make... one tap to confirm.' DR-50 itself rejects 'Dealing a card when a budget runs out: a spend cap isn't a decision only a person can make.' The cost card is not defined anywhere in contracts.md: there is no `DecisionCard` cause or kind for it.
findings.failure_scenario: In `keys.test.tsx::main_flows_within_two_keys`, the S3 flow runs the 'priorities' stage, which is the fifth row under `i`. The presses are row key `9`, then `Enter`, then `1` on the cost card: 3 presses after the list is open, or 4 counting `i`. Handing off the third next action takes `7`, `h`, then the deliberate confirm: 3 presses. The test fails, or it gets weakened to count only the first row, and S9 (tier B) ships as a gap. The person pays one extra interruption on every one of the six stages.
findings.proposed_fix: In pane focus, which is a deliberate surface with no stray-digit risk, let Enter on a stage row run the stage directly. Show its estimate inline in the row ('≈4.5k tok, cached'), and deal a cost card only when the estimate would cross the remaining budget or the provider has no consent yet. For repo-changing steps, make the row key surface that row's card face-up, so that the action key, for example `h` or the card's choice digit, is itself the deliberate second key. That gives select-the-card then confirm, two presses. Define the cost card in contracts (its cause, and when it is dealt). Extend `main_flows_within_two_keys` to run a non-first stage and hand off a last-row item.

findings.title: The owner's edits from an unpaired phone are discarded by the pre-selected one-tap answer
findings.claim: Unsigned rows under the owner's uid go into one confirming card with 'No' pre-selected, and inbox docs are deleted after import. Nothing says the declined rows are kept or that the No can be undone. So taking the cheapest action, confirming the pre-selected pick, silently destroys work the person did on their phone. KICKOFF names one user, so these rows are usually the person's own edits.
findings.evidence: architecture.md:1346: 'The owner's unsigned rows ... apply nothing ... They become one card the local person confirms: "Apply 3 edits and 1 pick from an unpaired device?", with No pre-selected.' contracts.md:901: `inbox/<uid>/events/<docId>` is 'deleted after import'. contracts.md:902: `acks/<uid>` marks rows `imported | conflict | refused`, and the page stops showing them as queued once they're acked. DR-67 Amended: 'the card for unsigned owner rows pre-selects No'. Neither architecture.md nor contracts.md says where a declined row's request is stored or how to get it back. KICKOFF principle 1: 'Never lose or overwrite what someone did. Everything is reversible, which is what makes bold defaults safe.' A default is safe only when it can be reversed.
findings.failure_scenario: The owner regroups three blocks and picks a card on their phone, which was never paired, and then runs `/room sync` at the desk. Import deletes the inbox docs and deals the card. The owner presses the pre-selected pick: No. The acks mark the rows refused, the phone shows them as gone, and nothing in the store holds their requests. The work is lost with no undo. S15's 'every edit type has an undo test' doesn't cover it, because no edit was ever written.
findings.proposed_fix: At import, store every unconfirmed row as a ghost (provenance `artifact-unsigned`, actor `person:artifact:<uid>`, cause the import) instead of deleting it with no record, so it shows in Diffs like any proposal. 'No' then means 'reject these ghosts', which `edit undo` reverses like any review. Alternatively, make the card's pre-selected choice 'Keep as proposals' rather than discarding. Add `s11_remote.rs::a_declined_unpaired_row_is_kept_and_undoable`, and have the acks report `held` rather than `refused` for these rows.

findings.title: Some agent-facing outputs have no size budget, and type discovery returns the whole schema
findings.claim: Several commands that agents read have no output budget ('n/a'): `schema`, `schema --commands`, `doctor --json` and `export`. Pack questions may declare any `budget_tokens`, or none. The flat tool inputs send agents to `planroom schema --commands` or `room help` for request types, so an agent that needs one leaf's shape has to pull the whole catalogue or schema into context. That breaks 'every agent-facing output has a size budget' and 'never return a raw file when a pointer or slice will do'.
findings.evidence: architecture.md:1200, the CLI table: `export`, `schema [--commands]`, `doctor ...`, `version` all have Default budget `n/a`. `doctor --json` carries 'the last 50 log lines, redacted, so `doctor --json` is the bug report's attachment'. contracts.md:839: 'The description holds one generated synopsis line per leaf, and `room help` or `planroom schema --commands` gives the full request types.' contracts.md QuestionDecl: `budget_tokens: Option<u32>`, with no cap stated for an out-of-tree pack. The error registry's `invalid_argument` details hold only `field`, with no pointer to the leaf's type. KICKOFF principle 2, Token-efficient: 'every agent-facing output has a size budget; answers come summary-first, with handles to drill down; never return a raw file when a pointer or slice will do.'
findings.failure_scenario: An agent calls `room_change` with `command: intent` and `args: ["propose"]`, and its payload has the wrong field name. It gets `invalid_argument {field}`. To learn the shape it follows the documented route and runs `scripts/planroom schema --json` through Bash. That pulls both schema views, which will be tens of KB for about 60 `$defs`, into context on every such recovery. Or the S10 toy pack declares `budget_tokens = 50000` for a question, and an agent's `ask` returns an unpaged 50k-token blob. Neither case is gated by `budgets.rs`, which covers only the S2 questions and S3.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `schema --command LEAF` and `schema --def NAME`. Each returns only that leaf's request and result types with their `$defs` closure, summary first, under a budget of about 1,500 tokens. Put that exact handle in `invalid_argument`'s `hint` and `details.schema`. Give `schema` and `schema --commands` a budget, with paging and handles per leaf, plus a pointer to the committed schema file path for the full document. Make `doctor --json` return a summary with the log as a path. Clamp pack `budget_tokens` to the kernel's `show` ceiling (3,000), and fall back to the `ask` default when it is unset. Add a test asserting that every catalogue leaf has a non-n/a budget, or is a stream or file export that returns a pointer.

findings.title: Nobody is assigned to re-run a command after the session broker fills its model request
findings.claim: On the session backend, which most plugin users have because they have no gateway key, a Claude-using command returns a pending `ModelRequest` together with a re-run handle. The mod's broker fulfils the request and imports the response, but nothing says who then re-runs the command. A stage started from the pane or the canvas can therefore spend the session's tokens and show nothing until someone repeats the action.
findings.evidence: architecture.md:906: '... then `planroom import` of a `planroom.model-response/v1` file ... so re-running the command picks it up; each `meta.model_requests` entry carries that exact re-run handle.' architecture.md:1020: pane Enter runs `intent next --stage S`. DR-18 and DR-21 say the same and assign no owner for the re-run. feature_list S3 evidence: 'once with the session backend ($.model.complete)'. KICKOFF principle 1: 'Never show a blank state', and 'at a fraction of the effort'.
findings.failure_scenario: The person presses Enter on the 'outcome' stage in the pane. `intent next` returns a pending request, and the broker completes it and imports the response. But nobody re-runs `intent next`, so no ghosts land and the pane still shows the old card. The person presses Enter again, which is now a cache hit and finally produces the proposals. An agent that called `intent next` through a tool also has to poll the handle, spending a turn.
findings.proposed_fix: Make it the broker's job: after a successful `import` it runs each request's `rerun` handle with the original actor, client and cause, and the original `idem` suffixed `#rerun`. While the request is pending, the pane and canvas show an engine-authored 'Drafting outcome with your Claude session…' state. Add `packages/mod/src/broker.test.ts::fulfilled_request_reruns_its_handle`.

findings.title: Tool inputs pass arguments as untyped strings
findings.claim: To meet the 900-token tools budget, each mod tool takes `command` plus `args: string[]`. The schema the model sees types none of a leaf's parameters, so 'typed interfaces' holds for the CLI and HTTP API but not for the tools agents mostly use. Mistakes surface only as clap parse errors after a round trip.
findings.evidence: contracts.md:828-837: `"args": { "type": "array", "items": { "type": "string" } ... }`. DR-66 records the trade-off for the token budget. KICKOFF principle 2: 'Every capability is reachable through stable, typed, documented interfaces ... tools agents can call'.
findings.failure_scenario: The chat model sends `room_query {command: "ask", args: ["path", "storefront->worker"]}`. Nothing in the tool schema rejects it, so the engine returns `invalid_argument` with only `field`. The model guesses again and burns a second call, and its tokens, on each S2 question.
findings.proposed_fix: Keep the flat shape, but have `invalid_argument` from a tool carry the leaf's one-line synopsis and the `schema --command LEAF` handle (see principles-4) in `hint` and `details`. Add a golden test showing that a wrong-argument call to each leaf returns its synopsis within the error budget. Optionally, register a deferred `room_typed` tool with full per-leaf `oneOf` types for agents that load it on demand.

findings.title: Model consent is split across several cards, and their defaults contradict each other
findings.claim: A workspace can deal separate consent cards for Jev on the gateway, TypeSafe, Claude on the gateway and the session backend, on top of the per-user Jev setup card, so these are not batched. The setup card tells the person to 'Set AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY', but the consent card that follows pre-selects No for 'a credential found only in the environment'. A person who follows Planroom's own instructions must therefore override Planroom's own default.
findings.evidence: architecture.md:920: consent is 'per workspace and provider ... Yes is pre-selected for the session backend and for a credential the user-level config names for Planroom; for a credential found only in the environment, No is.' architecture.md:1000: the setup card reads '"... Set AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY", with the exact steps'. KICKOFF principle 1: 'pre-decided, batched ... Never ask what a good default could answer.'
findings.failure_scenario: The person sees the setup card, exports `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` as it instructs, and rescans. A Jev consent card now appears with No pre-selected. Their one tap keeps Jev off, which is the opposite of what they just chose, and a Claude-on-gateway consent card arrives later as a separate interruption.
findings.proposed_fix: Have the setup card's steps write the key into the user-level config (mode 0600), which pre-selects Yes, or record the person's setup choice as consent intent so the next consent card pre-selects Yes. Batch every pending provider consent for a workspace into one card with a pick per provider, dealt once.

findings.title: Every person write from a terminal costs an extra /dev/tty confirmation
findings.claim: A person at a terminal with no `PLANROOM_ACTOR` gets a read-then-confirm on `/dev/tty` for every write, including routine reversible edits. Typing the command already expressed the decision, so this is an interruption that a default could answer for people who use the CLI.
findings.evidence: architecture.md:422: 'A person at a terminal with no `PLANROOM_ACTOR` gets a read-then-confirm: the CLI reads the target, prints what it's changing and at which `seq`, reads the confirmation from `/dev/tty`'. KICKOFF principle 1: 'Make those decisions cheap ... Never ask what a good default could answer'; 'Everything is reversible, which is what makes bold defaults safe.'
findings.failure_scenario: A person renames, regroups and hides five blocks from a shell: five commands and five extra confirmations, all for edits with an `Edit` undo class.
findings.proposed_fix: Ask on /dev/tty only for `Compensate`-class or person-only commands. For `Edit`-class writes, apply them and print the `edit undo` handle. Alternatively, let one /dev/tty confirmation grant a short terminal-scoped person lease, recorded and revocable, that covers later `Edit`-class writes from that tty.

verdicts.reason: The resolver is a hand-written sh script that prints public JSON: the engine_fetching and engine_unavailable envelopes, and status --json, which feeds the mod's engine atom. No codegen produces that output and no schema validation covers it. The contract row says so outright. The registry tests are scoped to Rust CLI output, and the one-place-for-codes rule can't hold while sh spells two codes. This breaks the KICKOFF constraint 'One contract source ... CLI --json output ... with a drift test', so it is material.
verdicts.evidence: contracts.md:70, 'Resolver environment and status': single source `plugin/scripts/planroom` and the table, codegen targets `none`, and the only tests are behavioural installer tests. contracts.md:150: '`contract::ErrorCode` is the only place a code is spelled; a source scan fails on a code string anywhere else.' contracts.md:173-174 make engine_fetching and engine_unavailable 'the resolver's envelope'. contracts.md:995 limits `every_cli_json_output_validates` to 'every envelope the test suite produces'. architecture.md:1427: the sh resolver 'exits non-zero with one envelope, `engine_fetching`'. contracts.md:867: the `engine` atom is fed by 'the resolver's `status --json`'. No document under review has a generated shell constants file or a validation test for resolver output.

verdicts.reason: As written, the design can't meet its own S9 assertion. Running a stage from the pane takes `i` (or a row key), then Enter, then the cost card's pick. That is three presses even for the first row, and four for a later row. feature_list S9 asserts both 'at most two real key presses ... on any visible row' and 'Enter on a stage row under i runs intent next --stage S through its cost card, within two keys from pane focus', and those can't both hold. Ranking the needed row first doesn't help, because S9 explicitly tests the last visible row. No contract defines the cost card. S9 is tier B, so this is material.
verdicts.evidence: architecture.md:1020: 'Enter on a stage row runs `intent next --stage S`. That can spend, so the engine deals its cost card first and the card's pick confirms it.' architecture.md:1268: 'A row key selects its row, and an action key then acts on the selected row ... at most two keys'. architecture.md:1269: a repo-changing or paid step 'opens its card in the pane, where confirming takes a second, deliberate key'. feature_list.json S9 asserts 'at most two real key presses from pane focus, on any visible row' and includes 'acting on the last visible row of each list'. KICKOFF:173: 'Every action is at most two keystrokes from pane focus.' A grep finds no cost-card definition in contracts.md.

verdicts.reason: Unsigned owner rows become one card with No pre-selected, and the inbox docs are deleted after import. No document under review says where the declined rows' requests are kept or how to apply them later. Generic decision overrides do exist (picked -> overridden; `decide <id> <choice>`), but this card has no defined kind or effect. Kernel effects are a closed set of six, and none is 'apply imported rows', so there is no evidence the override path can bring them back. One tap on the default can therefore lose the person's phone edits. That conflicts with 'Never lose or overwrite what someone did. Everything is reversible.' It is a data-loss risk, so it is material.
verdicts.evidence: architecture.md:1346: unsigned owner rows 'apply nothing ... They become one card ... with No pre-selected'. contracts.md:901: `inbox/<uid>/events/<docId>` is 'deleted after import'. contracts.md:902: acks mark rows `imported | conflict | refused`. contracts.md:939 repeats the rule and says nothing about storage. architecture.md:856: 'effect is a closed set of six kernel effects'. architecture.md:819/944 allow overriding a pick in general, but nothing ties that to these rows. KICKOFF:39-40.

verdicts.reason: The CLI table gives `export`, `schema [--commands]`, `doctor` and `version` a 'n/a' budget. `doctor --json` carries 50 log lines. The tool docs send agents to `schema --commands` or `room help` for request types, and `schema --commands` only lists `$ref`s, so getting a leaf's shape means pulling the full schema. QuestionDecl.budget_tokens is an unbounded Option<u32>, and no document under review states a cap for pack questions. These outputs are agent-facing, so this breaks KICKOFF principle 2, 'every agent-facing output has a size budget; ... never return a raw file when a pointer or slice will do'. That makes it material.
verdicts.evidence: architecture.md:1200, the `export`, `schema [--commands]`, `doctor`, `version` row: budget n/a, with 'the last 50 log lines, redacted, so `doctor --json` is the bug report's attachment'. architecture.md:1188: `ask` budget 'per question'. contracts.md:285: `schema --commands` gives 'the `$ref` of its request and result types'. contracts.md:839: '`room help` or `planroom schema --commands` gives the full request types'. contracts.md:609: `budget_tokens: Option<u32>`. contracts.md:153: invalid_argument details are only `field`. KICKOFF:44-47.

verdicts.reason: The gap is real. The session backend gives each request a re-run handle, and the broker imports the response, but no document under review makes anyone responsible for re-running the command, and no surface shows a pending state for it. It fits the reviewer's MINOR rating: the person can repeat the action and get a cache hit, so no tier A or B scenario fails outright.
verdicts.evidence: architecture.md:906: '... then `planroom import` ... so re-running the command picks it up; each `meta.model_requests` entry carries that exact re-run handle.' contracts.md:104: `rerun: Handle`. DR-18 (decisions.md:426): 'the command picks it up when re-run'. architecture.md:1243: a model_request 'starts the session broker'. None of these says the broker or the pane re-runs the command.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed as minor. Tool inputs are a `command` enum plus untyped `args: string[]`, and invalid_argument carries only `field`, with no synopsis or schema handle for the leaf. DR-51/DR-66 record this as a deliberate token trade-off, and the clap tree validates the arguments, so the cost is an extra round trip, not a failing scenario.
verdicts.evidence: contracts.md:828-837: the flat schema with `"args": {"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"}}`. contracts.md:839: 'The engine parses `command` and `args` with the same clap tree as the CLI, so validation and errors are the CLI's.' contracts.md:153: invalid_argument `details` is `field` only.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed as minor. The setup card tells the person to 'Set AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY', with 'Keep deterministic' pre-selected. A key found only in the environment then gets a consent card with No pre-selected. Consent is per provider, and no document under review batches the cards. The No default for an ambient key has a security reason, but nothing makes the setup card's steps lead to a Yes-defaulted path. This is friction, not a scenario failure.
verdicts.evidence: architecture.md:920: 'Consent per workspace and provider. The providers are Jev on the gateway, TypeSafe, Claude on the gateway, and the session backend ... Yes is pre-selected for ... a credential the user-level config names for Planroom; for a credential found only in the environment, No is.' architecture.md:1000: the setup card '... Set AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY', with the exact steps, and 'Keep deterministic' pre-selected. The documents never say what the steps are or whether they write the user-level config.

verdicts.reason: Real and minor. Every terminal write without PLANROOM_ACTOR goes through a read-then-confirm on /dev/tty. The confirmation does more than ask: it supplies the CAS base, and it tells a person apart from an agent that has no tty. So it isn't purely redundant, and simply dropping it (the finding's first fix) would weaken person attribution. The finding's other fix, a short revocable tty-scoped lease, would keep that. Still, nothing in the documents under review lets a person batch these confirmations or skip them for Edit-class writes, and it affects no tier A or B scenario.
verdicts.evidence: architecture.md:422: 'A person at a terminal with no `PLANROOM_ACTOR` gets a read-then-confirm: the CLI reads the target, prints what it's changing and at which `seq`, reads the confirmation from `/dev/tty`, and commits with that base as `person:<os-user>`.' architecture.md:415: the terminal confirmation is a person path, and 'Anyone who controls a pty can confirm that prompt'.
